scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which falls outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Camila Perez and I'm 80. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello Ms. Perez, I'm sorry to hear about the confusion regarding your billing. I can certainly look into this for you. Could you please provide your account number and the email address associated with the service?
Sure, my account number is 8849201 and the email is cperez80@email.com.
Thank you. Just to confirm, can you also provide the zip code on file for your account?

Thanks. I see the account here. Per our standard terms of service, refunds are typically restricted to requests made within 30 days of the charge. Since you are slightly past that window, I'll need to check if I can make an exception here.
I understand the policy, but I really wasn't home to check my statements. Is there any way to waive that for me?

I understand your situation. Given that it is only a few days past the window, I am going to go ahead and process this refund for you as a one-time courtesy. I have submitted the request to our billing department now.

resolution_summary: The agent processed the refund as a one-time courtesy despite the request falling outside the 30-day policy window.

judge_scores.justification: The agent verified the customer's identity with appropriate account details and maintained a warm, polite tone throughout the interaction. Furthermore, the agent correctly cited the 30-day policy before using their authority to apply a one-time courtesy exception, resulting in a smooth and successful resolution.
